original_question: Consider the space of monic polynomials z maps to z^n + a_{n-1} z^{n-1} + ... + a_1 z with |a_1| >= 1, so that the origin is an unattractive fixed point, and do not assume the Julia set is connected. If at least one external ray lands at the origin, there is a rotation number for these rays under theta maps to n theta mod 1. Does this rotation number extend uniquely to a continuous map from this space of polynomials to R/Z, taking the value theta when a_1 = e^{2 pi i theta}?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation. It matches the exact family of monic polynomials with zero constant term, the condition |a_1| >= 1 so that 0 is a nonattracting ('unattractive') fixed point, the fact that connectedness of the Julia set is not assumed, the hypothesis that at least one external ray lands at 0, the induced angle map theta -> n theta mod 1, and the normalization that when a_1 = e^{2 pi i theta} the sought map should take the value theta.
missing_details: The degree n should be understood as fixed, and implicitly n >= 2.
The coefficients a_j are complex; equivalently, the parameter space is the coefficient space X_n = {z^n + a_{n-1}z^{n-1} + ... + a_1 z : a_j in C, |a_1| >= 1}.
The continuity is with respect to the usual coefficient topology on X_n.
The rotation number is only initially defined on the subset of X_n consisting of polynomials for which at least one external ray lands at 0.

To make the question fully stand-alone, 'external ray' should be understood in the usual polynomial-dynamics sense (a dynamic ray in the basin of infinity), which is important because the Julia set is not assumed connected.
refined_question: Fix an integer n >= 2, and let X_n be the space of monic complex polynomials P(z) = z^n + a_{n-1}z^{n-1} + ... + a_1 z with |a_1| >= 1, endowed with the usual coefficient topology. For every P in X_n, the origin is a nonattracting fixed point, and the Julia set of P is not assumed to be connected. On the subset of X_n for which at least one external (dynamic) ray lands at 0, let rho(P) in R/Z denote the well-defined rotation number of the external rays landing at 0 under the angle map theta -> n theta mod 1. Does rho extend uniquely to a continuous map X_n -> R/Z, normalized by the condition that whenever a_1 = e^{2 pi i theta}, the extended map has value theta mod 1?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s Question 12 in §2 almost verbatim. The exact phrasing appears immediately after Question 11 and the sentence 'Here is a different kind of continuity question,' in the subsection on quasiconformal surgery. The nearby §2 context also supplies the intended dynamical setting in which ray-rotation numbers are being discussed, namely the intertwining-surgery discussion involving rays landing at periodic points with a specified rotation number. There is no different nearby official formulation that is sharper than this one; the right refinement is simply to make the parameter space, topology, and domain of the partially defined rotation-number map explicit without broadening the problem.
